hero.headline: Anthropic Valued Above OpenAI After $65 Billion Funding Round
hero.body:
Anthropic has surpassed OpenAI in valuation following a major funding announcement. The AI company raised $65 billion in Series H funding, reaching a post-money valuation of $965 billion and claiming the title of world's most valuable AI startup.

The funding round was led by Altimeter Capital, Dragoneer, Greenoaks, and Sequoia Capital. Anthropic's ascent marks a significant shift in the competitive dynamics of the artificial intelligence industry. The company, which develops Claude, a large language model that competes directly with OpenAI's GPT models, has transformed from being perceived as a smaller player in the global AI race into a dominant force.

Much of Anthropic's rapid growth stems from widespread enterprise adoption of its products. The company gained particular traction following the release of coding assistants and tools like Claude Code and Cowork. Krishna Rao, Anthropic's chief financial officer, stated that "Claude is increasingly indispensable to our growing global community of customers, and we work tirelessly to make tools like Claude Code and Cowork more helpful, more powerful, and more adaptable to their needs."

Anthropic's business strategy has focused on enterprise and coding services rather than consumer-facing products. The company has also distinguished itself through its emphasis on AI safety. One of Anthropic's cofounders participated in Pope Leo's recent release of an extensive document warning against the dangers of artificial intelligence and calling for greater restrictions on the technology.

The company has maintained its safety commitments despite government pressure. Anthropic engaged in a legal dispute with the Pentagon after refusing to remove safeguards from Claude that would enable use in mass surveillance or autonomous weapons systems capable of killing without human intervention. Reports indicate the U.S. government has nonetheless used Claude for military operations.

Anthropic recently withheld the release of its Mythos model due to cybersecurity concerns, prompting international alarm about potential vulnerabilities to financial systems and critical infrastructure. Vice President JD Vance contacted AI company leaders urging greater cooperation on security matters.

The company has also become an influential political force, investing millions in lobbying efforts and political action committees supporting candidates and legislation aligned with its regulatory vision for artificial intelligence. Unlike other tech industry leaders and OpenAI, Anthropic advocates for increased government oversight of AI development.

The record valuation reflects continued investor confidence in AI despite public skepticism about the technology. This comes after OpenAI raised $122 billion in March to achieve a valuation of $852 billion, with reports suggesting the company may pursue a $1 trillion initial public offering later this year.

cards.headline: Trump requests changes to Iran nuclear deal after envoys reach tentative agreement
cards.body:
President Trump asked for several amendments to a nuclear agreement his envoys negotiated with Iranian counterparts during a Situation Room meeting on Friday, according to administration officials and sources briefed on the discussions.

Trump wants the deal finalized soon but is seeking to strengthen specific provisions, particularly those related to Iran's nuclear material, two U.S. officials said. His requested changes have launched another round of negotiations that could extend for several more days.

The tentative agreement reached this week would extend the current ceasefire and potentially reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway for global oil transport. If approved, the deal would mark significant progress in ongoing negotiations between Washington and Tehran aimed at resolving regional tensions.

Trump announced Friday that he would convene the Situation Room meeting, and his announcement suggested he was leaning toward accepting the agreement. However, the president's review led to his request for modifications to specific terms before moving forward.

The amendments Trump requested focus on strengthening nuclear-related provisions, though the exact details of the proposed changes were not disclosed. Trump's involvement signals both his interest in securing an agreement and his determination to ensure the final terms meet his administration's objectives.

The negotiations come amid broader diplomatic efforts between the U.S. and Iran. Senior U.S. and Iranian envoys previously met in Oman for talks that addressed Iran's nuclear program. However, broader issues including Iran's ballistic missile program and its support for regional allies remain points of contention, with Israel calling for additional restrictions on these areas.

Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu met with Trump earlier this week in a three-hour meeting at the White House. Netanyahu's office had indicated he wanted any negotiations to include limits on Iran's ballistic missiles and reductions in Iranian support for groups including Hamas and Hezbollah. Trump stated in an online post that he had told Netanyahu that pursuing a deal was his preference, but that other options remained available if negotiations failed.

Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian has said his country is willing to negotiate over its nuclear program and is "ready for any kind of verification" to demonstrate it is not seeking nuclear weapons. However, the International Atomic Energy Agency has been unable to inspect and verify Iran's nuclear stockpile for months.

Trump's envoys initially presented their negotiated agreement to the president for review before his Situation Room meeting. The back-and-forth between parties is expected to continue as negotiators work to incorporate Trump's requested changes. Officials indicated the president remains committed to finalizing an agreement despite seeking amendments to the current draft.

cards.headline: Zelensky warns of major Russian attacks within 48 hours
cards.teaser: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said he expects Russia to launch major attacks within the next two days based on intelligence from U.S. and European allies.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky is preparing for a major Russian attack expected within the next 48 hours, based on intelligence from U.S. and European allies. He indicated the strikes could occur tonight or tomorrow night.

The warning underscores ongoing Russian military operations against Ukraine and reflects Western assessments of Russian military preparations and movements in the region.

cards.headline: UN blacklists Israeli and Russian forces for sexual violence in conflict
cards.teaser: The United Nations added Israeli and Russian security forces to its annual list documenting sexual violence during conflict, including allegations of rape against detained Palestinians.
cards.body:
The United Nations has added Israeli and Russian security forces for the first time to its annual blacklist documenting sexual violence during conflict, including allegations of rape against detained Palestinians. The report released on a recent date lists 77 government and non-government parties in countries credibly suspected of patterns of rape or other forms of sexual violence.

The inclusion of Israeli and Russian forces marks the first time either has appeared on the U.N.'s annual list. The designation is based on credible allegations of sexual violence committed by security forces from both countries during military operations and detention.

cards.headline: 11 Dead After Tank Explosion at Washington Paper Mill
cards.body:
Eleven people died in an explosion at a paper mill in Longview, Washington. Recovery crews have retrieved all victims from the site, and authorities have confirmed their identities.

The disaster occurred at Nippon Dynawave Packaging Co. on Tuesday morning when an industrial tank ruptured and released white liquor, a highly corrosive chemical mixture used in paper manufacturing. Officials initially reported one death and nine injuries. As recovery operations continued, one hospitalized victim died, bringing the total death toll to 11. Seven workers remained hospitalized following the incident.

Governor Bob Ferguson stated at a news conference that the state was "bracing ourselves for this being the deadliest industrial tragedy in modern Washington state history."

The tank held approximately 600,000 gallons of liquid composed mainly of sodium hydroxide and sodium sulfide. White liquor is used with heat to break down wood into kraft paper, a durable material used for packaging and shopping bags. About 25,000 gallons remained in the damaged tank and slowly leaked into a drainage ditch.

Recovery operations began Wednesday following delays caused by structural safety concerns with the damaged tank. Matt Amos of the Longview fire department said recovery efforts would be "slow, methodical and deliberate." Crews performed decontamination procedures on recovered victims before transport to the coroner, and responders worked in chemical protective equipment throughout operations.

The chemical spill contaminated a drainage ditch and entered the Columbia River on Tuesday. Dead carp were found in the water. Authorities advised the public to avoid ditches and dikes in the area while water testing continued. However, officials reported no air quality or drinking water concerns in Longview.

The US Chemical Safety and Hazard Investigation Board announced it would launch a federal investigation into the incident. The Washington state department of ecology and the US Environmental Protection Agency oversaw operations to assess environmental impacts.

The sprawling Longview facility employs approximately 1,000 people and manufactures material for tissues, printing paper, cups, plates and cartons. It sits along the Columbia River near other timber, paper and chemical businesses.

Prior to the explosion, safety complaints were filed against Nippon Dynawave in March and May. The state's labor and industries department stated both complaints were unrelated to the current situation. One involved an anonymous complaint about a tank valve, though it was not the tank that imploded. Since 2021, the company had been fined $3,400 for three separate health and safety violations found by state inspectors.

Brian Wood with Nippon Dynawave said the company was focused on victims and would cooperate fully with the investigation. "These are our people," he stated at a news conference. The facility remains closed as investigators examine the scene to determine what caused the tank failure.

cards.headline: Ebola outbreak in Congo kills more than 245 people
cards.body:
More than 245 people are now suspected to have died from Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo, with health officials confirming 65 deaths so far. The outbreak, centered in Ituri province, has prompted urgent international coordination as the virus spreads across borders.

The World Health Organization estimates the death rate between 30 and 50 percent based on confirmed cases. "It means that up to five out of 10 people are likely to die," said Anaïs Legand from the WHO's high threat pathogens team.

There have been 246 suspected cases reported in Ituri province, a conflict-affected region that shares borders with Uganda and South Sudan. Uganda has already confirmed cases, including a 59-year-old man who died in a Kampala hospital after traveling from the DRC. Cases have been reported mainly in the Mongwalu and Rwampara health zones, with suspected cases also appearing in the neighboring city of Bunia.

The medical charity Médecins Sans Frontières warned that the spread of the virus is deeply alarming. The WHO director visited the region worst affected by the outbreak to support containment efforts.

Health workers in affected areas lack adequate equipment to respond to the crisis. Aid organizations are racing to provide resources and support. The situation is complicated by the location's challenging circumstances. Ituri province is a mining hub where thousands of people work in close proximity daily, and it remains a conflict zone with ongoing fighting between rebel groups. Displaced people are being forced into overcrowded camps to escape the violence, making disease control even harder.

The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention detected the Ebola virus in 13 of 20 samples tested. Notably, the virus identified is the Bundibugyo strain, for which there is no licensed vaccine. This differs from the Zaire strain typically seen in previous DRC outbreaks. Only two prior outbreaks of Bundibugyo virus have occurred, in 2007 and 2012.

The DRC has experienced 16 Ebola outbreaks since the virus was first identified there in 1976. Experts point to several factors behind these recurring epidemics. Close human contact with animal reservoirs, particularly bats and possibly primates, creates risk. The movement of people between rural and urban environments, combined with the tropical climate and extensive rainforest coverage, enables transmission.

International health organizations are coordinating with Congolese authorities, Uganda, and South Sudan to deploy medical teams and supplies. The Africa CDC is convening urgent meetings with pharmaceutical companies to address the outbreak. Efforts focus on isolating patients, tracing contacts, and providing treatment to those infected.

The regional spread underscores the need for rapid coordination. "Given the high population movement between affected areas and neighbouring countries, rapid regional coordination is essential," said Dr Jean Kaseya, director general of Africa CDC.

cards.headline: Blue Origin Rocket Explodes at Florida Launch Complex
cards.teaser: Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket exploded at Launch Complex 36 in Florida, hours after the company received a national security launch contract.
cards.body:
A Blue Origin New Glenn rocket exploded during a hotfire test at Cape Canaveral in Florida on Thursday night at 9pm ET. The massive fireball destroyed the launchpad, with the orange sky visible as far south as Fort Pierce, 115 miles away. No personnel were harmed, according to the company, which called the incident an anomaly.

The explosion threatens NASA's lunar plans, which depend on the New Glenn rocket for its moon base construction and crewed return missions scheduled for the next two years. The incident came just hours after Blue Origin received a national security launch task order from the government. The company later regained access to the launchpad.

cards.headline: Five freed from flooded cave in Laos after more than a week trapped
cards.teaser: Rescuers freed five people from a flooded cave in Laos after they were trapped for over a week.
cards.body:
Four more miners trapped in a flooded cave in Laos for 10 days have been freed by divers, bringing the total rescued to five. The men were among seven villagers who entered the narrow tunnels on May 20 in search of gold. Two people remain missing as rescue teams continue navigating through muddy water, sharp rocks, and narrow passages.

The rescue operation has proven extremely hazardous, requiring teams to drain water from the cave and manage collapse risks. One person was successfully rescued on Friday, followed by the extraction of four more miners in subsequent operations.

cards.headline: Hundreds arrested in France after Champions League celebrations turn violent
cards.teaser: More than 280 people were arrested in Paris as celebrations of PSG's Champions League victory erupted into clashes.
cards.body:
Thousands of police officers deployed across Paris to manage unrest as fans celebrated Paris Saint-Germain's Champions League victory over Arsenal. Some supporters fired flares during the street gatherings.

Authorities arrested more than 280 people as violence erupted throughout the city. The arrests occurred as crowds of fans took to the streets following the match, with police working to control the celebrations.

cards.headline: Drone crashes into apartment building in Romania near Ukraine border
cards.teaser: A drone struck an apartment building in eastern Romania, bringing the Russia-Ukraine war close to civilian homes.
cards.body:
Residents of an eastern Romanian apartment building experienced a loud explosion and fire when a drone crashed into their building. The incident reminded people living near the border that the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war poses risks to neighboring countries.

The crash caused panic among residents as the war entered civilian spaces in Romania. Romania shares a border with Ukraine, placing some communities in proximity to the ongoing conflict between Russia and Ukraine.

cards.headline: Israeli soldiers describe ongoing killings in Gaza despite ceasefire
cards.teaser: Israeli soldiers gave rare firsthand accounts from Gaza, saying killings continue despite a ceasefire agreement.
cards.body:
Israeli soldiers have provided rare public accounts to the Associated Press about their experiences in Gaza, with one soldier describing the ceasefire as "a joke" and indicating that killings have continued. These testimonies offer uncommon insight into military operations in the region.

An Israeli commander separately stated that Hezbollah had planned attacks on Israel comparable to those carried out by Hamas on October 7th.

cards.headline: Japan defense minister rebuts China's accusations of militarism
cards.teaser: Japan rejected claims of new militarism from China and accused Beijing of rapidly expanding its own military.
cards.body:
Japan's defense minister rejected China's accusations of militarism, arguing that Japan remains a peace-loving nation while China expands its military capabilities without sufficient transparency. The comments were made during a speech at a regional security forum.

Under Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, Japan has accelerated a shift toward a more active defense policy, moving away from the pacifist stance it has maintained since World War II. The defense minister pledged to continue strengthening the military despite Beijing's criticism of Japan's increasingly assertive security approach.

cards.headline: Ecuador offers to cancel tariffs after call with Colombian candidate
cards.teaser: Ecuador's president said he would cancel tariffs after speaking with a right-wing candidate in Colombia's election.
cards.body:
Ecuadorian President Daniel Noboa offered to cancel tariffs after speaking with a right-wing presidential candidate ahead of Colombia's Sunday election. The move drew criticism from those who view it as foreign interference in the Colombian electoral process.

The gesture has sparked accusations that Ecuador is inappropriately involving itself in Colombia's democratic proceedings. Critics argue that such offers from a neighboring leader to a specific candidate undermine the integrity of the election.

cards.headline: Protesters Clash With Police at New Jersey Immigration Facility
cards.teaser: Protests at Delaney Hall in Newark turned violent after the governor called for calm.
cards.body:
Demonstrations continued outside Delaney Hall, an immigration detention center in Newark, New Jersey, as a hunger and labor strike by detained immigrants entered its ninth day. The detainees were demanding improved conditions and medical care.

On Saturday, the facility became a flashpoint between opposing groups. Supporters of the detained immigrants faced off against counterprotesters wearing Trump hats who demonstrated in support of ICE operations. State police set up barricades to separate the two groups as they clashed outside the facility. Newark Mayor Ras Baraka imposed a mandatory curfew for the area within half a mile of the center.

cards.headline: Judge Blocks Trump Plans to Rename and Close Kennedy Center
cards.teaser: A federal judge halted the administration's proposed changes to the performing arts venue in Washington.
cards.body:
A federal judge blocked plans by the Trump administration to add the president's name to the Kennedy Center and to close the performing arts venue for renovations. The ruling prevented the planned closure and renaming of the facility.

Trump criticized the judge who issued the decision and expressed frustration over the legal setback. The Kennedy Center, a cultural institution in Washington, will remain open and retain its current name. The administration had proposed renovations that would have required shutting down the venue.

cards.headline: Trump Sends Revised Terms to Iran After Initial Deal Negotiated
cards.teaser: The president requested changes to the framework his envoys had agreed to with Iranian officials.
cards.body:
President Trump met with his advisers to make a final determination on a peace framework that U.S. and Iran officials had agreed upon. After reviewing the initial agreement, Trump requested edits and sent tougher terms back to Iran.

The president has not yet announced a final decision on the deal. Defense Secretary Hegseth discussed the negotiations publicly. The proposed agreement addresses an ongoing conflict now in its 92nd day.

cards.headline: Four Inmates Escape Alabama Correctional Facility
cards.teaser: Authorities are searching for prisoners who broke out of a detention center.
cards.body: Four inmates escaped from a correctional center in Alabama. Authorities launched a search for the prisoners who fled the facility. The search involves multiple law enforcement agencies working to locate and apprehend the four individuals.

cards.headline: Bus Driver Charged After Crash Kills Family of Four Headed to Wedding
cards.teaser: Five people died in a collision in Virginia, including a family traveling to a wedding.
cards.body:
A crash in Virginia killed five people, including a family of four who were traveling to a wedding. The bus driver involved in the collision has been charged.

Authorities arrested the bus driver following the fatal accident. The family was on their way to attend a wedding when the crash occurred.

cards.headline: Meteor Explosion Over Massachusetts Triggers Loud Boom
cards.teaser: A meteor exploded in the atmosphere above New England, causing reports of loud noises.
cards.body:
A meteor exploded over northeastern Massachusetts and southeastern New Hampshire on Saturday afternoon, creating sonic booms that reverberated across the region. NASA confirmed the blast was equivalent to 300 tons of TNT.

The meteor was traveling at 75,000 miles per hour when it broke apart at an altitude of 40 miles above Earth's surface. The explosion generated loud booms heard throughout the northeastern United States.

cards.headline: China Factory Activity Contracts Further
cards.teaser: Manufacturing activity in China weakened further, raising concerns about the trajectory of the world's second-largest economy.
cards.body:
Factory activity in China worsened in the latest reporting period, according to Bloomberg. The decline signals growing challenges for the Chinese economy as manufacturing activity continues to contract.

The weakening factory data adds to concerns about China's economic outlook. Manufacturing has been a key pillar of Chinese growth, and sustained contraction in the sector points to broader economic headwinds facing the country.

cards.headline: SoftBank Plans Up to $75 Billion Investment in French AI Data Centers
cards.teaser: SoftBank announced plans to invest up to 75 billion euros to build what would be Europe's largest AI facility in France.
cards.body:
SoftBank announced plans to invest up to €75 billion to build artificial intelligence data centers in France. The project aims to develop and operate up to 5 gigawatts of additional data center capacity, positioning France to host Europe's largest AI infrastructure facility.

This investment marks a significant expansion of AI computing resources in Europe, supporting the continent's artificial intelligence development and applications.

cards.headline: United Airlines Flight Diverted After Passenger Allegedly Attempts Cockpit Breach
cards.teaser: A United Airlines flight from Chicago to Minneapolis was diverted after a passenger allegedly tried to breach the cockpit, triggering a hijacking alert.
cards.body:
United Airlines flight 2005 traveling from Chicago to Minneapolis made an emergency landing in Madison after a passenger allegedly attempted to access the cockpit. The incident forced the aircraft to divert and prompted a hijacking alert.

The passenger was arrested following the emergency landing. The FBI stated that no criminal charges had been filed yet as the investigation continued. The disruption affected passengers bound for Minneapolis who were rerouted through Madison.

cards.teaser: Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket exploded at Launch Complex 36 in Florida, hours after the company received a national security launch contract.

cards.headline: Ferrari Faces Criticism Over First Electric Vehicle Design
cards.teaser: Ferrari's first electric vehicle, the Luce, drew sharp criticism from some who say the design abandons the brand's traditional roots.
cards.body:
Ferrari unveiled the Luce, its first electric vehicle intended to compete with Chinese EV manufacturers. The launch generated a wave of negative responses from critics who argued the vehicle represents a departure from Ferrari's heritage.

The backlash centered on design choices that some Ferrari enthusiasts found incompatible with the brand's identity. Ferrari positioned the Luce as its answer to the growing electric vehicle market, particularly the expansion of Chinese EV makers into the luxury segment.

cards.headline: New Car Sales Drop for Eighth Consecutive Month
cards.teaser: The American new car market lost approximately one million buyers, with sales declining for the eighth straight month as demand weakens.
cards.body:
New car sales in the United States fell for the eighth consecutive month, with approximately one million buyers exiting the market. The prolonged sales decline reflects reduced consumer demand and affordability challenges facing potential car buyers.

Electric vehicle demand has weakened as part of the broader slowdown. Automakers have maintained profitability despite the sales crash, according to industry reports. The data suggests that purchasing a new car has become increasingly difficult for many American consumers.

hero.headline: Meteor explodes over Massachusetts, creates loud sonic boom
hero.body:
A meteor exploded over northeastern Massachusetts and southeastern New Hampshire on Saturday afternoon, triggering sonic booms that reverberated across a wide swath of the northeastern United States. NASA confirmed the event occurred just after 2pm local time.

The fireball was traveling at 75,000 miles per hour at an altitude of 40 miles when it broke apart in the atmosphere. The explosion produced a blast equivalent to 300 tons of TNT, according to NASA's deputy news chief Jennifer Dooren.

Reports of the event came from a vast geographic area. Witnesses across New England, from Delaware to Montreal, reported hearing the mysterious loud boom. Residents in the Boston area and throughout Massachusetts described the sound and vibrations that initially puzzled many who experienced it.

The meteor's fragmentation in the atmosphere explains why the explosion was so widely heard without corresponding reports of impact damage. When meteors are large enough and enter at the proper angle, the extreme heat and pressure of atmospheric entry can cause them to fragment violently, producing powerful sonic booms audible across multiple states and into Canada.

The event took place over a populated region, making it particularly notable due to the number of witnesses. Social media quickly filled with reports from residents trying to determine the source of the mysterious sound.

Meteors entering Earth's atmosphere occur regularly, but most burn up quietly at high altitudes or over unpopulated areas. When a meteor breaks apart at lower altitudes over populated regions, it becomes more noticeable to residents on the ground.

Weather monitoring systems and seismic equipment likely recorded the event. No injuries or property damage were reported from the meteor explosion.

The widespread nature of the sonic boom demonstrates the power of atmospheric friction on large space objects. As meteoroids descend through increasingly dense layers of air, they experience mounting pressure and heat. Eventually, for larger objects, this stress becomes too great and the meteor shatters explosively.

Any fragments that survived atmospheric entry would be scattered over a wide area, making them extremely difficult to locate. Most material burns up completely during the violent descent.

The event serves as a reminder that Earth is constantly bombarded by space debris. According to NASA, most space rocks smaller than a football field will break apart in the atmosphere. Though rare, some explode in the air rather than burning up silently.

Larger meteors capable of producing sonic booms audible over such extensive geographic areas occur regularly on a global scale. This event highlighted how visible and dramatic these cosmic encounters can be when they happen over populated regions during daylight hours when many people are outdoors or near windows.

cards.headline: First Windows PCs with Nvidia chips to debut next week
cards.teaser: The first Windows computers powered by Nvidia processors will be unveiled next week, marking a significant shift in PC chip architecture.
cards.body:
Nvidia, Microsoft, and Arm have teased an upcoming announcement at Nvidia's GTC event showcasing new Nvidia N1X laptop processors designed to power Windows PCs. This marks the first time Nvidia chips will be used in Windows machines, breaking from the traditional reliance on Intel and AMD processors in the Windows market.

The collaboration signals a significant shift in the PC industry landscape. Nvidia's Arm-powered chips are positioned as ready for launch, with the companies building anticipation through social media messages ahead of the formal reveal.

cards.headline: SoftBank to invest up to 75 billion in French data centers
cards.teaser: The Japanese technology firm announced plans to develop and operate significant new data center capacity in France.
cards.body:
SoftBank plans to invest up to €75 billion to build data centers across France, with the goal of developing and operating up to 5 gigawatts of additional capacity in the country.

The investment marks a significant expansion of data infrastructure in Europe. Data centers provide the computing systems and networking equipment essential for cloud services and internet operations.

cards.headline: AC releases new Cobra coupe with 720 horsepower
cards.teaser: The British car manufacturer unveiled a production model of its iconic sports car with a supercharged V8 engine.
cards.body:
AC has revived the iconic Cobra nameplate with a new GT Coupe, a two-seat sports car powered by a Ford 5.0-liter V8 engine. The vehicle delivers between 720 and 799 horsepower depending on its configuration, positioning it as a high-performance supercar.

The coupe design marks a departure from the classic open-top roadster versions of the Cobra. Production models are priced from $315,000 to $500,000 based on specifications chosen by buyers.

cards.headline: New James Bond game '007: First Light' records strong first-day sales
cards.teaser: The video game launched with significant 24-hour sales figures and positive reception from players and critics.
cards.body:
Developer IO Interactive has crafted '007: First Light' as a prequel following a young Bond in his pre-00 days. The studio, known for its Hitman assassination series, shifts its familiar formula to explore Bond's formative years rather than taking an easier adaptation route.

IO Interactive brings its signature strengths to the project: globetrotting locations, attention to luxury and architectural detail, and its in-house Glacier engine. The developer's experience creating games about a besuited protagonist navigating high-stakes scenarios provides a natural foundation for reimagining the iconic spy character.

cards.headline: Blue micromoon visible this weekend
cards.teaser: The second full moon of May, known as a blue moon, will be visible over the coming nights.
cards.body:
This weekend offers a rare chance to observe a blue micromoon in the night sky. Despite its name, the moon won't actually appear blue or particularly small.

A blue micromoon combines two lunar phenomena. A blue moon is the second full moon occurring within a single calendar month. A micromoon happens when the full moon coincides with the moon being at or near its farthest point from Earth in its orbit, making it appear smaller and dimmer than usual. Together, these events create a relatively uncommon celestial occurrence worth watching for clear skies this weekend.

cards.headline: Nintendo releases new compatibility fixes for Switch games on Switch 2
cards.teaser: The gaming company issued another wave of updates to improve how original Switch games run on the newer console.
cards.body:
Nintendo released a new set of backwards compatibility fixes for Switch games running on the Switch 2 console. The updates address issues that occur when playing games designed for the original Switch on the newer hardware.

Backwards compatibility allows owners of the Switch 2 to play games from the previous generation console. Nintendo has been releasing periodic fixes to improve the performance and functionality of these older games on the new system.

hero.headline: Claude Lemieux dies at 60, family to donate brain for CTE research
hero.body:
Four-time Stanley Cup champion Claude Lemieux has died at 60, and his family has decided to donate his brain for chronic traumatic encephalopathy research.

Lemieux won Stanley Cup championships throughout his National Hockey League career. He played as a right winger known for his physical style of play.

The family announced their decision to donate Lemieux's brain to scientists studying CTE, a degenerative brain condition associated with repeated head trauma. The condition has been found in numerous former professional athletes, particularly in contact sports like hockey and football.

CTE can only be definitively diagnosed after death through examination of brain tissue. Researchers have been working to understand the condition's progression and its connection to symptoms including memory loss, confusion, depression, and changes in behavior.

Lemieux's brain donation will contribute to ongoing medical research into the long-term effects of head injuries sustained during professional sports careers. Scientists continue to study the brains of former athletes to better understand how repeated impacts affect brain health over time.

The hockey community has been mourning the loss of Lemieux, who built a reputation as a playoff performer during his years in the NHL. His four Stanley Cup victories came during a career that spanned multiple teams and decades.

Brain donation by former athletes and their families has become increasingly common as awareness of CTE has grown. These donations provide crucial data for researchers attempting to develop better diagnostic tools and potential treatments for the condition.

Lemieux's death and his family's decision to support CTE research highlight ongoing concerns about player safety in professional hockey and other contact sports. The NHL and other leagues have implemented various rule changes and protocols in recent years aimed at reducing head injuries, though the long-term effects of careers played before these changes remain a subject of medical study.

cards.headline: Spurs advance to NBA Finals after Game 7 win, Wembanyama named West Finals MVP
cards.teaser: Victor Wembanyama led the San Antonio Spurs past the defending champion Thunder in Game 7 to reach the NBA Finals.
cards.body:
Victor Wembanyama led the San Antonio Spurs to a 111-103 victory over the Oklahoma City Thunder in Game 7 of the Western Conference Finals, earning him Western Conference Finals MVP honors. The win sends San Antonio to the NBA Finals for the first time in years, dethroning the defending champion Thunder.

The Spurs will face the New York Knicks in the championship series, with Game 1 scheduled for Wednesday in San Antonio. This marks another Finals matchup between these two franchises, who previously met in the 1999 NBA Finals.

cards.headline: Knicks and Spurs set for NBA Finals matchup
cards.teaser: The New York Knicks will meet the San Antonio Spurs in the NBA Finals after both teams advanced through their conference championships.
cards.body:
The San Antonio Spurs defeated the reigning champion Oklahoma City Thunder 111-103 in Game 7 of the Western Conference Finals, securing their spot in the NBA Finals. Victor Wembanyama led the Spurs to victory and was named Western Conference Finals MVP.

The Spurs will face the New York Knicks in the championship series, with Game 1 scheduled for Wednesday in San Antonio.

cards.headline: Brighton manager Vidosic aims to honor late father in Women's FA Cup final
cards.teaser: Brighton manager Dario Vidosic will lead his team against Manchester City in the Women's FA Cup final with personal motivation.
cards.body:
Brighton manager Dario Vidosic will face Manchester City in Sunday's Women's FA Cup final at Wembley with his late father in mind. Vidosic's father, Rado, who served as the women's team's head of coaching, died from cancer four months ago.

Growing up in Brisbane, Vidosic cherished memories of staying up past his bedtime to watch major Wembley finals alongside his father, then recreating memorable goals together in the garden. As Brighton pursue their first major trophy, Rado will be remembered by the entire club during the final.

cards.headline: Hundreds arrested in France after Paris Saint-Germain Champions League celebrations
cards.teaser: French police arrested hundreds of people as PSG fans celebrated their Champions League victory over Arsenal.
cards.body:
Thousands of police officers were deployed across France as Paris Saint-Germain fans celebrated the team's Champions League victory over Arsenal. The large crowds gathered throughout the country to mark PSG's retention of the title.

During the celebrations, some fans fired flares as police worked to manage the unrest. The deployment of thousands of officers was necessary to control the crowds and maintain order during the post-match festivities.

cards.headline: Arsenal to hold Premier League parade day after Champions League final loss
cards.teaser: Arsenal will celebrate their Premier League title with an open bus parade less than 24 hours after losing the Champions League final.
cards.body:
Arsenal will celebrate their first Premier League title in 22 years with an open bus parade on Sunday, just hours after losing the Champions League final to Paris Saint-Germain on penalties. Kai Havertz gave Arsenal an early lead in Budapest, but PSG equalized through Ousmane Dembélé in the second half, forcing extra time.

Manager Mikel Arteta acknowledged the heartbreak of Gabriel Magalhães skying a penalty in the shootout, but urged the team to channel their disappointment into motivation. Despite falling short in Europe, Arsenal will honor their domestic championship achievement as they look ahead to next season.

cards.headline: Darren Till wins BKFC debut with knockout after being dropped early
cards.teaser: Former UFC fighter Darren Till secured a knockout victory in his Bare Knuckle Fighting Championship debut against Aaron Chalmers.
cards.body:
Darren Till made a successful debut in bare knuckle fighting, defeating Aaron Chalmers with a knockout. The reality television star caught Till early in the fight, dropping him to the canvas. Till recovered from the knockdown and mounted a comeback.

Till finished the bout with a vicious knockout blow to secure the victory in his Bare Knuckle Fighting Championship debut. The former UFC fighter's transition to bare knuckle boxing proved successful in his inaugural appearance.

hero.headline: Frankie Valli Cancels Remainder of Four Seasons Farewell Tour Over Health Concerns
hero.body:
Frankie Valli has canceled the remaining dates of the Four Seasons farewell tour to focus on his health. The 92-year-old music legend announced the decision Saturday, apologizing to fans in a statement.

Valli expressed regret over the cancellations. According to reports, he told fans he was sorry to disappoint them. The statement indicated he needed to prioritize his health for the remainder of 2026.

The tour was billed as a farewell for the Four Seasons, the vocal group Valli has fronted for decades. The group became famous in the 1960s with hits that later became the basis for the Broadway musical Jersey Boys.

Valli had been performing concerts throughout the year as part of the farewell tour. Multiple shows scheduled for the coming months have now been canceled. Fans who purchased tickets will presumably receive refunds, though specific details about ticket logistics were not provided in the announcement.

The singer's age and the demands of touring appear to have factored into the decision. At 92, Valli is among the oldest active touring performers in popular music. The physical requirements of sustained performance schedules can be taxing even for younger artists.

Valli's career has spanned more than six decades. He and the Four Seasons recorded numerous chart-topping songs beginning in the early 1960s. The group's popularity endured through multiple generations, receiving renewed attention after Jersey Boys debuted on Broadway in 2005.

No additional medical details were disclosed in the announcement. Valli did not specify what health concerns prompted the cancellations or whether he plans to return to performing in the future. The statement focused on the immediate need to step back from touring obligations.

cards.headline: Search Suspended for Man Believed to Be Alaskan Bush People Star Matt Brown
cards.teaser: Authorities suspended a search for a man believed to be reality television personality Matt Brown after reports that he took his own life.
cards.body:
Law enforcement has suspended their search for a man believed to be Matt Brown from the Discovery Channel series Alaskan Bush People. According to reports, the man took his own life near a river where police said a man had gone missing.

Brown appeared on the reality series, which documented his family's life in remote Alaskan wilderness. The show ran for multiple seasons and attracted a substantial viewership before Brown departed from the program several years ago.

cards.headline: Two YouTube Creators Direct Top Box Office Films
cards.teaser: The two highest-grossing films at the box office this weekend were both directed by filmmakers who started on YouTube.
cards.body:
The films Backrooms and Obsession took the top two spots at the box office, both directed by creators who began their careers on YouTube. Obsession overtook The Mandalorian and Grogu to claim a top position. Industry observers described the success as a word-of-mouth sensation.

Warner Bros. Pictures chief Michael De Luca spoke about why the films were working at the box office during a session at the Produced By conference. He emphasized the importance of pursuing new talent and fresh voices. De Luca warned that cutting development funds too deeply could dry up the pipeline for original material.

cards.headline: Love Island USA Removes Cast Member Over Racial Slur for Second Straight Year
cards.teaser: Peacock's Love Island USA dismissed a cast member after social media posts surfaced showing use of a racial slur, marking the second consecutive year the show has done so.
cards.body:
Love Island USA removed Vasana Montgomery from the upcoming season after social media posts emerged showing her using a racial slur. The reality dating series returns to Peacock on June 2. Montgomery will not appear in the season.

This marks the second consecutive year the show has dismissed a cast member for the same reason. Last year, another islander was removed from the villa after similar posts surfaced. The pattern raises questions about the show's vetting process for contestants before filming begins.

cards.headline: Niall Horan Reflects on Liam Payne's Death in New Interview
cards.teaser: The former One Direction member discussed his late bandmate's 2024 death, saying memories of their time together bring both sadness and laughter.
cards.body:
Niall Horan discussed the death of his former One Direction bandmate Liam Payne in an interview with The Times of London. Payne died in 2024 at age 31 following a fall from a hotel in Buenos Aires, Argentina. Horan described feeling sadness about the loss while also treasuring their shared memories together.

The two musicians had maintained their connection after One Direction went on hiatus, and Horan was in Argentina shortly before Payne's death. Horan reflected on their time together in the band, which rose to prominence in the 2010s before members pursued solo careers.

cards.headline: Morgan Wallen Flips Piano During Denver Concert
cards.teaser: The country singer overturned a piano onstage during a performance in Denver, apparently upset with the instrument.
cards.body:
Morgan Wallen flipped over a piano during a concert in Denver. The incident occurred while he was performing his song Sand in My Boots. Reports described Wallen as apparently upset with the instrument, though no specific reason was given for his actions.

Wallen has become one of country music's biggest commercial stars in recent years despite multiple public incidents. His albums have topped charts and broken streaming records. The piano-flipping incident drew comparisons to Billy Joel, who was known for similar stage antics earlier in his career.

cards.headline: Chad Gable Unmasked After Losing AAA Wrestling Match
cards.teaser: The wrestler known as El Grande Americano lost a mask versus mask match at AAA Noche de Los Grandes and was revealed as WWE performer Chad Gable.
cards.body:
Chad Gable was officially revealed as the wrestler behind the El Grande Americano mask after losing a mask versus mask match at AAA Noche de Los Grandes. The match took place Saturday and has been called a Match of the Year contender by wrestling observers.

The event featured multiple contests and drew attention from wrestling fans across promotions. Gable has performed primarily for WWE in

hero.headline: Trump requests changes to Iran nuclear deal after envoys reach tentative agreement
hero.body:
President Trump asked for several amendments to a nuclear agreement his envoys negotiated with Iranian counterparts during a Situation Room meeting on Friday, according to administration officials and sources briefed on the discussions.

Trump wants the deal finalized soon but is seeking to strengthen specific provisions, particularly those related to Iran's nuclear material, two U.S. officials said. His requested changes have launched another round of negotiations that could extend for several more days.

The tentative agreement reached this week would extend the current ceasefire and potentially reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway for global oil transport. If approved, the deal would mark significant progress in ongoing negotiations between Washington and Tehran aimed at resolving regional tensions.

Trump announced Friday that he would convene the Situation Room meeting, and his announcement suggested he was leaning toward accepting the agreement. However, the president's review led to his request for modifications to specific terms before moving forward.

The amendments Trump requested focus on strengthening nuclear-related provisions, though the exact details of the proposed changes were not disclosed. Trump's involvement signals both his interest in securing an agreement and his determination to ensure the final terms meet his administration's objectives.

The negotiations come amid broader diplomatic efforts between the U.S. and Iran. Senior U.S. and Iranian envoys previously met in Oman for talks that addressed Iran's nuclear program. However, broader issues including Iran's ballistic missile program and its support for regional allies remain points of contention, with Israel calling for additional restrictions on these areas.

Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu met with Trump earlier this week in a three-hour meeting at the White House. Netanyahu's office had indicated he wanted any negotiations to include limits on Iran's ballistic missiles and reductions in Iranian support for groups including Hamas and Hezbollah. Trump stated in an online post that he had told Netanyahu that pursuing a deal was his preference, but that other options remained available if negotiations failed.

Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian has said his country is willing to negotiate over its nuclear program and is "ready for any kind of verification" to demonstrate it is not seeking nuclear weapons. However, the International Atomic Energy Agency has been unable to inspect and verify Iran's nuclear stockpile for months.

Trump's envoys initially presented their negotiated agreement to the president for review before his Situation Room meeting. The back-and-forth between parties is expected to continue as negotiators work to incorporate Trump's requested changes. Officials indicated the president remains committed to finalizing an agreement despite seeking amendments to the current draft.

cards.headline: Zelensky warns of major Russian attacks within 48 hours
cards.teaser: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said he expects Russia to launch major attacks within the next two days based on intelligence from U.S. and European allies.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky is preparing for a major Russian attack expected within the next 48 hours, based on intelligence from U.S. and European allies. He indicated the strikes could occur tonight or tomorrow night.

The warning underscores ongoing Russian military operations against Ukraine and reflects Western assessments of Russian military preparations and movements in the region.

cards.headline: Justice Department seeks judge's recusal from Georgia election lawsuit
cards.teaser: Federal prosecutors asked a judge to step aside from the case against Georgia election officials, citing her attendance at an event honoring Fulton County District Attorney Fani Willis.
cards.body:
The Justice Department asked a federal judge to recuse herself from overseeing the department's lawsuit against Georgia election officials, arguing that her attendance at an event honoring Fulton County District Attorney Fani Willis raises questions about her ability to remain impartial. The filing was submitted to the U.S. District Court.

The recusal request centers on concerns that the judge's participation in the event could create an appearance of bias in the ongoing case. The Justice Department's lawsuit against Georgia election officials is separate from Willis's prosecutorial work, but the department argues the connection warrants the judge stepping aside.

cards.headline: UN blacklists Israeli and Russian forces for sexual violence in conflict
cards.teaser: The United Nations added Israeli and Russian security forces to its annual list documenting sexual violence during conflict, including allegations of rape against detained Palestinians.
cards.body:
The United Nations has added Israeli and Russian security forces for the first time to its annual blacklist documenting sexual violence during conflict, including allegations of rape against detained Palestinians. The report released on a recent date lists 77 government and non-government parties in countries credibly suspected of patterns of rape or other forms of sexual violence.

The inclusion of Israeli and Russian forces marks the first time either has appeared on the U.N.'s annual list. The designation is based on credible allegations of sexual violence committed by security forces from both countries during military operations and detention.

cards.headline: Lead prosecutor withdraws from Comey criminal case
cards.teaser: The federal prosecutor who secured an indictment against former FBI Director James Comey for allegedly threatening President Trump has stepped down from the case.
cards.body:
The federal prosecutor who secured an indictment against former FBI Director James Comey for allegedly threatening the life of President Trump in a deleted social media post of seashells has stepped down, according to a court filing. A notice of substitution filed in the Eastern District of North Carolina stated that Matthew, the lead prosecutor, is no longer on the case.

Comey faces criminal charges related to a social media post that prosecutors allege constituted a threat against the president. The post, which has since been deleted, featured seashells and was interpreted by authorities as threatening language.

cards.headline: New Jersey governor deploys state police to Newark ICE facility protests
cards.teaser: Gov. Mikie Sherrill deployed state police to maintain order outside a Newark immigration detention center that has seen escalating protests.
cards.body:
A hunger and labor strike by detained immigrants at Newark's Delaney Hall detention center entered its ninth day as protests intensified outside the facility. Demonstrators demanded improved conditions and medical care for those held inside.

State police set up barricades as competing groups gathered at the site. Pro-immigrant protesters faced off against Trump-supporting counterprotesters who showed up Saturday morning to demonstrate in support of ICE operations. Gov. Mikie Sherrill deployed state police to maintain order amid the escalating demonstrations.

cards.headline: Immigrant detainees sue over conditions at Texas ICE facility
cards.teaser: Detainees at Camp East Montana in El Paso, Texas filed a lawsuit accusing the federal government of inhumane abuse and treatment.
cards.body:
A class-action lawsuit filed Saturday accuses Immigration and Customs Enforcement of "dire" conditions at Camp East Montana in El Paso, Texas, the largest immigration detention facility in the United States. Four detainees filed the complaint on behalf of themselves and all current and future civil detainees at the facility.

The lawsuit alleges severe human and constitutional rights violations, including abhorrent medical and mental health care, inappropriate use of force, indiscriminate solitary confinement, inadequate food, disease outbreaks, unsanitary living conditions, and sexual harassment by guards. Legal organizations brought the class-action complaint against ICE over the conditions at the camp.
